newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China's Hainan cracks down on futures brokerages.
newsitem.headline: China's Hainan cracks down on futures brokerages.

text.p: Securities regulators in China's Hainan island are moving to step up supervision over the province's futures brokerages, the official Shenzhen-based Securities Times said on Wednesday.
The move was aimed at complying with Beijing's latest policy to further tighten controls on China's commodities futures market, the newspaper said.

The local securities regulatory body, the Hainan Securities Management Office, had required all futures trading agencies in Hainan to submit monthly reports on their operations to the authority, the newspaper said.
It quoted the office as saying it would also launch annual inspection into the financial situation of futures brokerages as well as their operations and risk controls.
Brokerages found to show poor results would face closure, it said. The office said it would accelerate closures of unlicensed brokerages to clean up the market.

The office emphasised that to standardise the market, financial institutions that had holdings in futures brokerages must transfer all stakes to non-financial ventures, but set no deadline for the order to divest.
